# Introduction

Social Media or the world we can't escape (even if we tried). No. Social media isn’t just a part of life anymore—it is the life. It’s where we scroll first thing in the morning, where we share our latest brunch photo, and where we go to laugh, learn, shop, and connect. It’s definitely a place where trends are born and brands are made. And let’s be honest: could you imagine a day without it? Probably not. We’re addicted, plain and simple.

Right now, digital communication dominates, and social media remains a cornerstone of marketing strategy. As we approach 2025, its relevance only amplifies. According to recent statistics, over 4.7 billion people are actively using social media platforms globally, with users spending an average of 2 hours and 31 minutes daily on these channels. That’s more time than most of us spend exercising, cooking, walking, or even reading!

Platforms like Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X.com, and Facebook have become our go-to spaces, not just for entertainment but for staying informed and building relationships. But social media isn’t just for selfies, chatting, and memes. It’s a goldmine for businesses, regardless of industry, location, or size. It is for anyone and everyone.

## Social Media by the Numbers

The scale of social media is mind-boggling. Consider these stats:

*   Instagram users post over 100 million photos and videos daily, excluding stories with 500 million daily active users.
*   LinkedIn sees around 8 million posts daily, sharing insights, jobs, and company updates.
*   TikTok users spend an average of 95 minutes daily watching and creating content, making it essential for younger audiences.
*   Facebook remains a giant with 2.9 billion monthly active users, where users upload 147,000 photos and make over 55,000 comments every minute.
*   X (formerly Twitter) users post 500 million tweets daily, offering a real-time pulse on news and trends.

## Curious How AI Agents Can Help?

After discussing AI agents extensively in previous blogs—how they developed, how they work, and their role in content creation—this blog will explore the top AI agents that can help marketers streamline their processes and create impactful social media. Let’s jump in:

## 11 AI Agents for Social Media Growth and Engagement

### 1\. Soshie (from Sintra AI)

**Overview:** Soshie is an AI-powered social media assistant designed to help you manage and grow your social media presence. It can create posts, plan campaigns, generate content, and handle social media tasks efficiently.

**Key Features:**

*   Task Automation: Performs over 15,000 tasks quickly, including creating content calendars and post ideas.
*   Image Generation: Create images with simple prompts.
*   Multi-Language Support: Works in over 100 languages.
*   Content Strategy Development: Builds tailored social media strategies.
*   Power-Ups Integration: Connects with platforms for advanced automation.

**Pros:**

*   Simple interface that’s easy for anyone to use.
*   Quick responses and 24/7 support.
*   14-day money-back guarantee for a risk-free trial.

**Cons:**

*   Limited beyond social media platform integrations.
*   Requires brand-specific input during setup.

## Conclusion

Consistency is the name of the game when it comes to social media success. Posting quality content on a regular basis keeps your audience engaged and aligns with algorithms to boost your brand’s visibility. Sticking to a posting schedule, crafting engaging content, and understanding your audience’s tastes can be overwhelming. But with the right social media agent, you can make it work for you.

# AI agents for social media: How to use them right now + what you can expect in the future

Written by: [Alex Sventeckis](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/author/alex-sventeckis)

![A blue hardcover book titled ](https://blog.hubspot.com/hs-fs/hubfs/Screenshot%202026-06-17%20at%205.41.32%20PM.png?width=112&height=112&name=Screenshot%202026-06-17%20at%205.41.32%20PM.png)

## SOCIAL MEDIA TRENDS REPORT

Explore the top trends in social media, along with opportunities, challenges, and new data to optimize social content.

[Download for Free](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)

![woman using ai agent for social media](https://blog.hubspot.com/hubfs/ai-agents-for-social-media-1-20250501-8542300.webp)

Updated: 10/06/26

 

I was running social media for an organization when [TweetDeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TweetDeck) hit the market. That dashboard with mentions, DMs, lists, and trends was the neatest piece of technology. I left it running in a tab 24/7 in between using it to plan our posts and stay abreast of our audience’s needs.

As I look at AI and how it’s influencing marketing and social media, it hits me just how far we’ve come. AI is already changing how I think about connecting with my audiences, creating content that reaches them, and competing in an extremely crowded online space to get my message heard.

[![Download Now: The 2026 State of Social Media Trends \[Free Report\]](https://no-cache.hubspot.com/cta/default/53/3dc1dfd9-2cb4-4498-8c57-19dbb5671820.png)](https://cta-redirect.hubspot.com/cta/redirect/53/3dc1dfd9-2cb4-4498-8c57-19dbb5671820)

[Agentic AI promises an even brighter future](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/AI-agents): an autonomous AI-powered tool that doesn’t just help you with tasks — it acts on its own within set guidelines. AI agents for social media management can watch for trends, respond to customers, and adjust your strategy on the fly.

How close are we to this future state? Let’s dive into what agentic AI looks like today and what tools are worth considering for your marketing team.

**Table of Contents**

*   [Can AI agents be used for social media?](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/ai-agents-for-social-media#can-ai-agents-be-used-for-social-media)
*   [Why use AI agents for social media management?](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/ai-agents-for-social-media#why-use-ai-agents-for-social-media-management)
*   [How to Use AI Agents for Social Media](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/ai-agents-for-social-media#how-to-use-ai-agents-for-social-media)
*   [Best Social Media AI Agents](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/ai-agents-for-social-media#best-social-media-ai-agents)[](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/ai-agents-for-social-media#where-ai-agents-fit-in-social-media-for-now)

## Can AI agents be used for social media?

In short? Yes. But it’s **probably not in the ways you expect.**

Despite the hype around agentic AI, few social media management platforms today offer true AI agents — the kind that listen, learn, and act without human approval. Right now, I’m seeing more agent-adjacent AI with powerful assistants that speed up workflows but that still require human direction.

More broadly, the bigger challenge rests on connecting agentic AI to “AI” as a concept within a business environment. [AI in marketing](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/AI-marketing) is an exciting but developing area, and people are racing to catch up. Generative AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini consume most of the oxygen in the AI discussion today.

And in marketing, you’re probably already experimenting with those models or [AI marketing bots](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/AI-marketing-bots) to generate specific content.

![](https://blog.hubspot.com/hs-fs/hubfs/Screenshot%202026-06-17%20at%205.41.32%20PM.png?)

### The State of Social Media in 2026

Explore the top trends in social media for brands to know and optimize your social strategy.

*   Community Building
*   Social Media Shopping
*   Social Vs. Search Engine

Marketers are moving fast, even as executives keep analyzing AI’s value and use cases. For instance, Salesforce’s 2024 [State of Marketing Report](https://www.salesforce.com/resources/research-reports/state-of-marketing/) found that 68% of marketing leaders say generative AI is “critical to their overall social strategy.” Our own research supports this finding, with one in three marketers already [deploying AI for content creation and data analysis](https://www.hubspot.com/state-of-marketing).

These AI use cases have generated customer-facing benefits for some companies. For example, Lyft partnered with Anthropic (makers of Claude) to automate elements of its customer support operations. Lyft reported an 87% reduction in [average customer service resolution times](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/ride-hailing-platform-lyft-ties-up-with-anthropic-ai-powered-customer-care-2025-02-06/%23:~:text%3DThe%2520company%2520said%2520it%2520has,of%2520customer%2520requests%2520each%2520day.) through all channels.

So, there is an emerging opportunity for AI agents to support social media management. But _should_ you use them? That answer is trickier.

Agentic social media AI can handle much of social media’s grunt work, things like monitoring sentiment, answering customer questions, or even defusing minor PR flare-ups before they trend (more on that later). If you run a human-only social media operation, you might already be falling behind.

**And the future will only get more agentic.** Gartner predicts that by 2029, [AI agents](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-03-05-gartner-predicts-agentic-ai-will-autonomously-resolve-80-percent-of-common-customer-service-issues-without-human-intervention-by-20290%23:~:text%3DGartner%2520Predicts%2520Agentic%2520AI%2520Will,Without%2520Human%2520Intervention%2520by%25202029) will autonomously handle at least 80% of customer service and support interactions — many of them taking place on social channels like Instagram, TikTok, and X/Twitter.

For marketers, then, it’s no longer _if_ you should use them, but _how smartly_ you use social media AI agent
